result.finding: The application has minimal security implementation. No authentication, authorization, HTTPS/TLS, or encryption features are configured. Spring Security is not a dependency. The web module includes only a request-logging interceptor (WebMvcConfig) and static resource caching. AWS credentials (access key, secret key) are stored as plaintext in application.properties, representing a significant security gap. The application has no CORS, CSRF protection, or security headers configured.
evidence: web/pom.xml and worker/pom.xml: spring-boot-starter-security is NOT present
web/WebMvcConfig.java: only a request-logging interceptor and static resource caching — no security filters
web/application.properties: AWS credentials (aws.accessKey, aws.secretKey) stored as plaintext — no secrets management
No @EnableWebSecurity, @PreAuthorize, JWT, OAuth2, or role-based access control annotations found in source code
No server.ssl.* properties or keystore configuration in application.properties
No CORS configuration in WebMvcConfig (no addCorsMappings method)
Production deploy script uses Azure Managed Identity (AZURE_CLIENT_ID) — passwordless authentication planned
values: Authentication: None (no Spring Security, no JWT, no OAuth2)
HTTPS/TLS: Not configured (HTTP only, HTTPS handled by Azure Container Apps ingress in production)
Encryption: None (credentials stored as plaintext in application.properties)
Security headers: None (no CORS, CSRF, HSTS, Content-Security-Policy)
Secrets management: None currently (migration target uses Azure Managed Identity)
